messages.subject: Setting parallel seed in plyr/foreach/doMC/multicore
parts:
I'm in the middle of a large simulation and need to ensure exact
reproduciblity so I have to set the seed.  It is a large simulation
and so I want to run it in parallel, as a check I ran this toy script.
---

> library(plyr)
> library(doMC)
> registerDoMC(3)
>
> set.seed(1)
> (a<-adply(c(4,4,4),1, rnorm, .parallel=T))
X1 V1 V2 V3 V4
1 1 -1.337354 1.2181139 0.01708719 -0.4392176
2 2 1.790212 0.4678536 -0.07931052 0.7596731
3 3 1.466294 -1.3375126 0.67054869 -0.6990728
>
> set.seed(1)
> (b<-adply(c(4,4,4),1, rnorm, .parallel=T))
X1 V1 V2 V3 V4
1 1 -0.4931063 0.6393119 0.6200816 0.1213044
2 2 -0.7760921 1.4855617 0.9134706 -1.3841006
3 3 0.5516576 -0.4817550 -0.5078418 -1.2787208
>
> stopifnot(all.equal(a,b))
Error: all.equal(a, b) is not all TRUE
---
unfortunately, this is not what I need. Is there a way to set the seed
for the parallel number generation? I am assuming that this is an
artifact of the multicore package which has no documentation I could
find on setting the parallel seed, only that it does set it if you
specify it to.

If the seed cannot be set has anyone figured out a work around with
either rlecuyer or rsprng?

thank you,
Andrew Redd

messages.subject: Re: Setting parallel seed in plyr/foreach/doMC/multicore
parts:
Hi Andrew-

I'm not totally clear on what you want, but it seems like writing a small function can give you what I think you want. The simple idea is that if you pass the seed as an argument, it sets it on the core instead of on the core that you are originally on. a multi argument call is mdply (returns your data frame)

rnorm.seed <- function( n, seed, ... ) { set.seed(seed); rnorm(n, ... ) }
mdply(data.frame(n=c(4,4,4), seed=c(1,2,3)), rnorm.seed, .parallel=TRUE )
  n seed         V1         V2         V3        V4
1 4    1 -0.6264538  0.1836433 -0.8356286  1.595281
2 4    2 -0.8969145  0.1848492  1.5878453 -1.130376
3 4    3 -0.9619334 -0.2925257  0.2587882 -1.152132
mdply(data.frame(n=c(4,4,4), seed=c(1,2,3)), rnorm.seed, .parallel=TRUE )
  n seed         V1         V2         V3        V4
1 4    1 -0.6264538  0.1836433 -0.8356286  1.595281
2 4    2 -0.8969145  0.1848492  1.5878453 -1.130376
3 4    3 -0.9619334 -0.2925257  0.2587882 -1.152132

HTH,
James

messages.author: 881c51ed14655bd5
messages.subject: Re: Setting parallel seed in plyr/foreach/doMC/multicore
parts:
here is one solution that I came up with that might be able to be integrated with plyr in general.  I hacked rlply to capture and store the seed of every iteration in foreach, then format them as a data frame that is stored as an attribute, similar to what plyr does with splitting labels.  This data frame could then be stored for easy replication of the simulation.  The problem with this solution is that the default random number generator is the Mersene twister that holds a random seed of length 626.  holding that for each replication might get too large.  I show it with the simplest random number generator.  It's not quite the same as setting the seed, but gets us closer.

---
> library(plyr)
> library(doMC)
> registerDoMC(9)
>
> my.rlply <- function(.n, .expr, .progress = "none", .parallel=F) {
+   if (is.function(.expr)) {
+     f <- .expr
+   } else {
+     f <- eval.parent(substitute(function(){
+ ._rng.seed_<-.Random.seed
+ structure({.expr},"._rng.seed_" =._rng.seed_)
+ }))
+   }
+
+   progress <- create_progress_bar(.progress)
+   result <- vector("list", length = .n)
+
+   progress$init(.n)
+   on.exit(progress$term())
+
+ if(.parallel){
+ if(!require("foreach")) stop("foreach package required for parallel plyr operation", call. = FALSE)
+ if(getDoParWorkers()==1) warning("No Parallel Backend Registered", call.=TRUE)
+ result <- foreach(i= seq_len(.n)) %dopar% f()
+ seeds  <- laply(result, attr, "._rng.seed_")
+ result <- llply(result, `attr<-`, '._rng.seed_',NULL)
+ result <- structure(result, seeds=seeds)
+   } else for(i in seq_len(.n)) {
+     result[i] <- list(f())
+     progress$step()
+   }
+   result
+ }
>
> RNGkind("Wichmann-Hill")
> l<-my.rlply(3, rnorm(4),.parallel=T)
> ldply(l, attr, '._rng.seed_')
data frame with 0 columns and 0 rows
> l
[[1]]
[1] -0.4114399 -0.2882785 -0.8333487 -0.4637808

[[2]]
[1] -2.4306794  0.3479854  0.5877466 -0.6728604

[[3]]
[1] -1.44624607  0.32791235  0.04124967 -0.48890279

attr(,"seeds")
       1     2     3     4
[1,] 400  4626 24602  5812
[2,] 400 25159  7713 21066
[3,] 400 23502 10340  5997
>
> #replicate
> m<-alply(attr(l,'seeds'), 1, function(seed){
+ .Random.seed<<-seed
+ rnorm(4)
+ }, .parallel=T)
>
> all.equal(l,m,check.attributes=F)
[1] TRUE
>
---

-Andrew

On Wed, Sep 14, 2011 at 10:35 AM, Andrew Redd <amr...@gmail.com> wrote:
That has been my thought to rig something up for that, but I'm tossing it out there to see if anyone has come up with a clever solution.

This basically boils down to the tug of war between repeatability and speed of parallel processes.  Since each iteration of my simulation should take about the same times I can save the list of seeds used to generate the different streams.  But there needs to be a complete solution if no one has found a way for it.

-Andrew
